stem: organic farming is an agricultural system in which -

options.label: a
options.text: Chemicals are used to the maximum extent as fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides

options.label: b
options.text: Organic fertilizers, recycled farm wastes and bio-agents are used in minimum quantities

options.label: c
options.text: Organic fertilizers, recycled farm wastes and bio-agents are used in maximum quantities

options.label: d
options.text: Growing two or more crops together in the same field

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In organic farming, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides is minimum (almost zero), while the use of organic manures, compost manure, agricultural wastes, biofertilizers (such as blue-green algae), etc. is maximum.

stem:
Which of the following is the correct example of organic fertilizer?
i. Mycorrhizal fungi
ii. Blue-green algae
iii. Bacillus thuringiensis

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Mycorrhizal fungi and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are examples of biofertilizers. Bacillus thuringiensis is a bacterium used in Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) cotton.

stem: Advancement occurs through the use of pesticides in terms of:
expl: By using fertilizers and pesticides, more crops and plants can be produced on less land. They help increase crop productivity. Pesticides also help maximize the benefits of other agricultural inputs such as water resources, fertilizers, and high-quality seeds.

stem: The parts of the skeleton that are not as hard as bones and which can be bent are called as

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Cartilage is a type of connective tissue in which there is sufficient space between the cells. Its solid matrix is made of chondrin (protein and sugar). It makes the joints of bones smooth; as a result, friction between bones is reduced. Cartilage is present in the nose, ear, larynx, trachea, and between the bones of the vertebral column. The study of cartilage is called chondrology.

stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about muscles in human body?

options.label: a
options.text: Muscles can only push the bone.

options.label: c
options.text: Muscles become shorter, stiffer and thicker when contracted.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Muscles help a person in activities such as walking, speaking, eating, etc. They assist in heartbeat, respiration, and digestion. Many other functions, including temperature, regulation and vision, also depend on the muscular system. Muscles work in pairs, and on contraction they become shorter, harder, and thicker. Therefore, the statement given in option (a) is incorrect.

stem: Muscle contains contractile proteins -
expl: Contractile proteins are involved in muscle contraction. Actin (thin filament) and myosin (thick filament) are the contractile proteins in muscles.

stem: in which organ of the human body is epithelial cells found?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Epithelial tissue is a thin and smooth membrane that covers the outer surfaces of all internal organs of the body. Epithelial tissue is found in various organs/parts of the body such as the tongue, kidney tubules, salivary glands, sweat glands, pancreas, lungs, nose, eyes, and ears.

stem: Glycogen stored in liver and muscles of the human body is in form of–

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Glycogen stored in the liver and muscles of the human body is a polysaccharide. Polysaccharides are carbohydrates available in abundance in food. When the body does not obtain sufficient energy from food, the body’s energy supply is met by converting stored glycogen into glucose.

stem: The number of bones in the hands and feet of an adult human, compared to the total number of bones in a human, is approximately what percentage?
expl: In an adult human, the total number of bones is 206, whereas the upper and lower limbs (extremities), i.e., the hands and feet, along with the girdles that connect them to the trunk, together have 126 bones; that is, about 60% of the total bones. Their distribution is as follows— (a) Upper (upper extremities) Pectoral (shoulder) girdles → 4 (b) Lower (lower extremities) Pelvic girdle → 2

stem: How many pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord?
expl: 31 pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord, whereas the number of cranial nerves is 12 pairs.

stem: The number of teeth that are developed twice in the lifetime of a human being is –
expl: In a human’s lifetime, 20 teeth develop twice, and 12 teeth develop only once.

stem: leg bone in the human body is –
expl: In the human body, the leg bone is solid.

stem: At the age of 20 years, the number of bones in the human body is approximately-
expl: The number of bones in the human body at 20 years of age is 206, which is mainly divided into two parts— Axial skeleton (80) Appendicular skeleton (126)

stem: Which of the following is not a vestigial organ in humans?
expl: From morphological and anatomical studies of organisms, we get knowledge about vestigial organs. A vestigial organ appears functionless, but it can be shown to be homologous to an organ that was functional in ancestors. For example, the vermiform appendix in the large intestine of humans, the nictitating membrane of the eye, and the auricular muscles of the pinna. Incisors are not vestigial organs.

stem: Which of the following connects a muscle to a bone?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A tendon connects muscle to bone. A tendon helps in the movement of the body’s bones/structures, whereas a ligament connects bone to bone.

stem: The type of joint found at the shoulder is also found at the

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In the above question, the joint found in the shoulder is also found in the hip.

stem: Which one of the following organs most actively functions to regulate our body temperature?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Among the options given in the above question, the skin works most actively to regulate our body temperature.

stem: Stapedius is a–
expl: Stapedius is the smallest muscle in the human body, located in the ears. It helps stabilize the stapes bone. It controls sound and protects the inner ear from damage due to loud noise.

stem: in the human system, insulin controls the metabolism of :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Insulin is produced by the pancreas. It is a hormone (a protein) that plays a major role in regulating glucose homeostasis. Insulin also stimulates the process of converting glucose into glycogen in target cells. Glucose is a form of carbohydrate.

stem: Energy is stored in liver and muscles in the form of :
expl: The cells of the body need energy to work. This energy is obtained from the chemical reactions of sugar, fat, and protein. Sugar gets converted into glucose in the body, which is a simple sugar. After absorption, it reaches different organs and tissues through the blood. In the liver and muscles, energy (glucose) is mainly stored in the form of glycogen.

stem: Which organ of the human body is affected by typhoid fever?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Disease Affected organ Typhoid (enteric fever), cholera Intestine Tuberculosis, plague, pneumonia Lung Tetanus, leprosy Nervous system Diphtheria, whooping cough Respiratory tract

stem: Which of the following human organ is affected by the consumption of aflatoxin food adulterant?
expl: The liver is a major digestive gland, which gets affected by food poisoning due to aflatoxins. Aflatoxins are toxic substances produced by certain fungi such as some species of Aspergillus and Penicillium, which make food poisonous.

stem: The source of the enzyme ‘lipase’ is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Most lipids in our food are present as simple fats, i.e., triglycerides. The enzyme lipase plays an important role in the digestion of lipids. It breaks lipids into fatty acids and monoglycerides. Lipase is naturally present in the juices secreted by the salivary glands, pancreas, and stomach. Bile has no digestive enzyme, yet it helps in the digestion and absorption of lipids. It emulsifies fats (emulsification). The enzyme pepsin helps in the digestion of proteins.

stem: The enzyme which is mixed with food in our mouth is

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Amylase is the main enzyme that mixes with food in the digestive system. Amylase is a type of enzyme or special protein that helps in the digestion of carbohydrates.

stem: Which of the following acid is secreted in the stomach ?
expl: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the parietal/oxyntic cells present in the stomach. It helps in the digestion of food, but if the acid is present in excess in the stomach, indigestion may occur. To get relief from indigestion, we take an antacid such as milk of magnesia, which contains magnesium hydroxide. It neutralizes the effect of excess acid.

stem: The sensitive area of the human tongue to bitterness is:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The front part of the human tongue experiences sweet taste, the back part experiences bitter taste, the side edges experience sour taste, and the front tip and edges experience salty taste.

stem: Which gland provides both endocrine and exocrine functions?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The pancreas is a mixed gland, having both exocrine and endocrine types of tissues or cells. The pancreas has two main functions— Exocrine—It mainly helps in the production of enzymes for the digestive system. Endocrine—It mainly regulates blood sugar.

stem: Which part of alimentary canal receives bile from the liver ?
expl: The liver is the largest gland of the human body. It is located just below the diaphragm, connected with the mesentery, and is deep reddish-brown in colour. Its weight is about 1.5 kg. It performs many functions. Some of its main functions are—production of bile, conversion of glucose into glycogen by the process of glycogenesis, etc.

stem: Which of the following is not an endocrine gland?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The lacrimal gland (tear gland) is not an endocrine gland. These glands are located above each eyeball, due to which tears are secreted in each eye. They are present in the upper outer (lateral) region of each eyeball. An endocrine gland is a ductless gland, which releases hormones directly into the blood. The organized endocrine glands in our body include the pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus, and the gonads.

stem:
Which of the following are not the tastes of the tongue?
1. Sweet 2. Bitter
3. Salty 4. Spicy
5. Umami 6. Sour
7. Pungent
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
expl: Sweet, bitter, salty, sour and umami are tastes of the tongue. Pungent and spicy are not tastes of the tongue. Umami taste is mainly obtained from food items like meat and eggs. Recently, scientists have proposed recognizing ammonium chloride as the sixth taste.

stem: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the above options, rice, wheat, barley, maize, etc. are major sources of carbohydrates. However, in 100 grams of cooked rice, the carbohydrate content is about 25.5 grams. In fact, about 90% of the calories in rice come from carbohydrates.

stem: The human body contains

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Most of our body is made up of water. In an adult human body, the amount of water is found to be about two-thirds (about 70%).

stem: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of which of the following vitamins?
expl: Pellagra is a disease caused by deficiency of vitamin B (niacin or nicotinic acid). In pellagra, the risk of diarrhea, skin-related disease, and confusion (dementia) increases.

stem: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Due to deficiency of vitamin ‘K’ (naphthoquinone), blood clotting becomes slow/delayed. This vitamin is called the antihemorrhagic vitamin. In persons with its deficiency, surgery cannot be performed easily because there remains a risk of excessive blood loss.

stem: Which of the following vitamins is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Vitamin ‘K’ is used as an antidote for anticoagulant poisons. This vitamin is called the antihemorrhagic vitamin. In persons with its deficiency, surgery cannot be performed easily because there remains a risk of excessive blood loss.

stem: in human body, Vitamin A is stored in :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the human body, a considerable amount of vitamin ‘A’ is stored in the liver. The chemical name of vitamin ‘A’ is retinol; its deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia. This vitamin is also called an anti-infective (infection-fighting) vitamin. Its main sources are milk, butter, eggs, fish oil, carrot, etc.

stem: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Deficiency of retinol, i.e., vitamin ‘A’, causes xerophthalmia. Deficiency of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B ) causes anemia, and deficiency of vitamin ‘D’ (cholecalciferol ‘D’ and ergocalciferol ‘D’) causes rickets in children. Beri-beri is caused by deficiency of vitamin ‘B’ (thiamine), not by deficiency of tocopherol (vitamin ‘E’).

stem: Which of the following vitamins is known as Ergocalciferol?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Deficiency of retinol, i.e., vitamin ‘A’, causes xerophthalmia. Deficiency of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B ) causes anemia, and deficiency of vitamin ‘D’ (cholecalciferol ‘D’ and ergocalciferol ‘D’) causes rickets in children. Beri-beri is caused by deficiency of vitamin ‘B’ (thiamine), not by deficiency of tocopherol (vitamin ‘E’).

stem: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sunlight and cod-liver oil are rich sources of Vitamin D. Wheat-germ oil is a major source of Vitamin E, while alfalfa contains Vitamin K in large amounts. Although orange is a major source of Vitamin C, it also contains Vitamin B in a very small amount. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

stem: Which of the following vitamins contain Cobalt –
expl: Cobalt is a mineral salt, which is an important component of Vitamin B (cyanocobalamin/cobalamin). Vitamin B is essential for growth, and its deficiency can also disturb the physiology of the nervous system. Important sources of Vitamin B are meat, fish, liver, milk, cheese, etc. Intestinal bacteria also synthesize it.

stem: Cobalamin is the scientific name of which of the following vitamins?
expl: Cobalt is a mineral salt, which is an important component of Vitamin B (cyanocobalamin/cobalamin). Vitamin B is essential for growth, and its deficiency can also disturb the physiology of the nervous system. Important sources of Vitamin B are meat, fish, liver, milk, cheese, etc. Intestinal bacteria also synthesize it.

stem: insulin is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above.

expl: Insulin is an animal hormone secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the endocrine part of the pancreas. From the viewpoint of chemical structure, it is a small peptide (protein) composed of 51 amino acids. It regulates glucose metabolism in the body and converts glucose into glycogen.

stem: Most of the enzymes are –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Enzymes are basically proteins, generally formed by the combination of nitrogenous substances or amino acids.

stem: The biological membranes are composed of:

options.label: a
options.text: Lipids and proteins in varying combinations which are specific to each species, cell type and organelle

expl: Biological membranes are mainly made of various combinations of lipids and proteins, which are specific to a species, cell type, and organ. According to the modern fluid mosaic model, the basic framework of the membrane is a phospholipid bilayer (lipid bilayer), in which different types of proteins are found floating or embedded.

stem: Substances which are responsible for catalyzing chemical reactions in living systems are -
expl: Enzymes are biological catalysts. They are generally proteins and, like other catalysts, increase the rate of reaction. In living organisms, most reactions occur in the presence of enzymes. As catalysts, they work in both forward and reverse directions. Therefore, they catalyze both the formation and breakdown of substances.

stem: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The chemical name of Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy. This vitamin is mainly found in citrus fruits and helps keep the skin clean and healthy. Vitamins B and C are water-soluble vitamins. Vitamins are organic compounds that regulate the metabolic activities of the body.

stem: Which vitamin is found in citrus fruits and is essential in keeping the skin healthy -
expl: The chemical name of Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy. This vitamin is mainly found in citrus fruits and helps keep the skin clean and healthy. Vitamins B and C are water-soluble vitamins. Vitamins are organic compounds that regulate the metabolic activities of the body.

stem: The chemical name of Vitamin C is-
expl: The chemical name of Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy. This vitamin is mainly found in citrus fruits and helps keep the skin clean and healthy. Vitamins B and C are water-soluble vitamins. Vitamins are organic compounds that regulate the metabolic activities of the body.

stem: Milk is a poor source of :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Milk is not a good source of Vitamin C, although it is rich source is calcium, protein and Carbohydrates.

stem: The malfunctioning of thyroid gland is due to the deficiency of :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Thyroxine, an iodine-containing hormone, is an amino acid, and it is secreted by the thyroid gland. The endocrine hormone that stimulates the thyroid gland to secrete thyroxine (T) is TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone), also called thyrotropin, which is secreted by thyrotroph cells of the anterior pituitary. When iodine and thyroxine levels in the blood decrease, secretion of TSH from the pituitary increases. Its effect is to stimulate the thyroid to secrete more and more hormones. Due to iodine deficiency in the body, a disease called goitre occurs.

stem: Which of the following is the best source of vitamin A?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Among the given options, carrot is the best source of Vitamin A. Other major sources of Vitamin A include green vegetables, milk, butter, egg, fish oil, etc. Diseases caused by Vitamin A deficiency include night blindness, xerophthalmia, dry, rough skin due to keratinization etc.

stem: Vitamin A is available in -
expl: Among the given options, carrot is the best source of Vitamin A. Other major sources of Vitamin A include green vegetables, milk, butter, egg, fish oil, etc. Diseases caused by Vitamin A deficiency include night blindness, xerophthalmia, dry, rough skin due to keratinization etc.

stem: Which of the following vitamins are water soluble ?
expl: The Polish scientist Casimir Funk first proposed the concept of vitamins and was the first to use the term “vitamin”. So far, about 13 types of vitamins are known, which are mainly classified into two categories— (i) Water-soluble vitamins: Vitamins B complex and C (ii) Fat-soluble vitamins: Vitamins A, D, E and K Vitamins are also called accessory food factors.

stem: yeast is used in the production of _____.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Yeast, mainly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is used for the production of alcoholic beverages like alcohol and beer because it converts the sugar of grains into ethanol. It is also used in the production of bread. It is also used as a nutritional supplement for humans.

stem: Which of the following activities increases oxygen in the carbon cycle occurring on Earth?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the process of photosynthesis, water and carbon dioxide are used and oxygen is released. Therefore, in the carbon cycle on Earth, photosynthesis increases oxygen.

stem: During expiration the diaphragm becomes

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The process in which fresh air from the atmosphere reaches our lungs and impure air comes out of the lungs is called breathing (Breathing). This process is completed in two parts— (i) Inhalation (Inspiration), (ii) Exhalation (Expiration). In exhalation (Expiration), carbon dioxide (CO)-rich air comes out of the lungs. In this, the ribs and diaphragm return to their normal position. The volume of the lungs decreases again. As a result, pressure on the lungs increases and carbon dioxide rich air is expelled from the body. During exhalation, the diaphragm is pulled upward and becomes dome-shaped.

stem: During normal respiration in mammals, the diaphragm is-

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In mammals, during inhalation (inspiration) the diaphragm becomes flattened. In fact, the diaphragm located below the lungs and spreading the thoracic and abdominal cavity is a respiratory muscle in mammals, which helps in the process of breathing.

stem: A clinical death takes place when

options.label: c
options.text: Pupils are fixed and dilated and there is no reaction to light

options.label: d
options.text: All the above three conditions are present together

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Clinical death is not actual death; it means , a person can be revived by CPR or other measures. Clinical death is declared when the following conditions are present together— → Pulse has stopped → Heartbeat has stopped → The pupils are fixed and dilated and show no reaction to light.

stem: in how many steps Co is released in aerobic respiration? 2

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: During aerobic respiration, carbon dioxide (CO) is released in three different stages. These stages are as follows— At the time of formation of Acetyl CoA (Acetyl-Coenzyme A), During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutaric acid, and During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of alpha ketoglutarate arale to (Succinyl-CoA).

stem: The most important cell type associated with the immunity of the body is

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Lymphocyte is the most important cell type related to the body’s immunity because it is the WBC that secretes the maximum amount of antibody proteins. Lymphocytes are formed in the bone marrow and are found in blood and lymphatic tissues. Lymphocytes are mainly of two types— B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. Notably, in response to pathogens, B-lymphocytes produce a chain of proteins in human blood so that they can fight pathogens. These proteins are called antibodies (Antibodies). T-lymphocytes do not secrete antibodies themselves, but they help B-lymphocytes in producing these proteins (antibodies). These are important parts of the immune system, which protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens.

stem: leukemia is a name for several types of cancer that originate in the bone marrow and cause a large number of abnormal blood cells to form. Which blood cell is this?
expl: Leukaemia is a group of blood-related cancers that originate in the bone marrow. In this condition, the number of white blood cells (WBCs) in the blood increases abnormally. WBCs are very important for the body’s immune system, as they protect the body from infections. In leukaemia, the abnormal white blood cells formed are not fully developed, and by crowding out normal blood cell formation, they weaken the body’s immune system.

stem: Which one of the following is used in the treatment of blood cancer?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Radio-phosphorus (P-32) and cobalt-60 are used in the treatment of leukaemia (a type of blood cancer).

stem: The total volume of blood in a normal adult human being is
expl: Blood is a liquid connective tissue. It continuously circulates inside blood vessels through different organs. In humans, the amount of blood is about 7 to 8 percent of body weight. Therefore, in a healthy adult of about 70 kg body weight, there are approximately 5 to 6 litres of blood, which is about one-thirteenth of the total body weight.

stem: The function of hemoglobin is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Haemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues and carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs. That is, the function of haemoglobin is to transport oxygen. Oxygen is required for blood circulation and for the functioning of all body organs, in which haemoglobin plays an important role.

stem: What prevents backflow of blood during heart contraction?

options.label: b
options.text: Thick muscular walls of the ventricles

expl: During heart contraction, the heart valves prevent the backflow of blood. The atria store blood and their walls are thin. The ventricles pump blood to different parts of the body. Since blood pressure is higher in the ventricles, their walls are thick.

stem: in transfusion, blood must be compatible not only in blood type, but also in -

options.label: d
options.text: race of the donor and recipient

options.label: e
options.text: none of the above / more than one of the above

expl: In blood transfusion, along with the blood group, the Rh factor must also be compatible. The Rh factor was discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener in the blood of the rhesus monkey.

stem: Which of the following instrument measures blood pressure –
expl: A normal human blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. There are two stages of blood pressure in arteries. The first is called systolic pressure and the second is called diastolic pressure. Generally, systolic pressure is 120 mmHg and diastolic pressure is 80 mmHg. Doctors measure blood pressure using a sphygmomanometer.

stem: in which organ of the human body are the lymphocytes formed?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the human body, lymphocytes are produced in the spleen, thymus gland, bone marrow, etc. Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cells (WBCs). They move throughout the body like a patrolling force and establish coordination among all parts of the immune system.

stem: Which among the following help in circulation of blood?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Erythrocytes (red blood corpuscles) generally help in the transport of oxygen in blood. Their main function is to carry oxygen from the lungs to all body tissues and to help in transporting apart of carbon dioxide back to the lungs.

stem: Blood group of an individual is determined by
expl: According to Mendel’s laws, a person’s blood group is determined on the basis of genes inherited from the parents. Its inheritance depends on genes/alleles of three (rather than two) contrasting characters.

stem: The universal acceptor blood group is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: A person with group O (O–) can donate blood to all groups; therefore, it is called the universal donor. It is worth noting that a person with AB group can receive blood of any group, but their blood cannot be given to a person of another blood group. Hence, a person with AB (AB+) is called the universal recipient.

stem: The blood group of universal donor is –
expl: A person with group O (O–) can donate blood to all groups; therefore, it is called the universal donor. It is worth noting that a person with AB group can receive blood of any group, but their blood cannot be given to a person of another blood group. Hence, a person with AB (AB+) is called the universal recipient.

stem: Myoglobin contains the metal –
expl: Myoglobin is an iron containing and oxygen-binding protein found in the muscles of vertebrates, whereas haemoglobin is found in blood (in red blood cells).

stem: The process of blood purification in the human body is called -
expl: The artificial process of blood purification in the human body is called dialysis.

stem: Which of the following is the fluid part of the blood ?
expl: Human blood is a fluid connective tissue. It supplies oxygen and nutrients to body tissues and carries CO and other waste products away from them. Blood has four components—plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Plasma constitutes about 55% of blood and the remaining components about 45%. Plasma contains mostly water (around 92%).

stem: Defective hemoglobin in the blood is seen in which of the following?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Sickle cell anemia is a genetic disorder. Due to this, red blood cells become sickle-shaped. It affects hemoglobin, which is a major protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Normally, red blood cells are biconcave and flow easily through blood vessels. This disease affects the hemoglobin molecule, changes the shape of red blood cells, and makes them sickle (crescent shaped) which can obstruct blood flow.

stem: lacteals are associated with which of the following?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Lacteals are lymph vessels present in the villi of the small intestine. They are similar to blood capillaries, but their diameter is larger than that of blood capillaries. Their main function is to absorb fats present in the digested food in the small intestine.

stem: The most important cell type associated with the body's immune system is -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Lymphocyte is the smallest white blood cell (WBC). Its main function is to destroy disease-causing organisms through immune responses and thereby increase the body’s immunity. Among all WBCs, it secretes the maximum amount of antibodies.

stem: in Tachycardia, the heart rate becomes

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Tachycardia is a medical term related to heart rate. When the heart beats 100 times or more in one minute, it is called tachycardia in medical science. In this condition, the heart rate becomes faster than normal. If the heart beats less than 60 times per minute, it is called bradycardia.

stem: The average blood flow through kidneys per minute is –
expl: The kidney is an important organ of the human body. Its main function is to purify the blood and remove toxic substances from the body through urine. Human kidneys filter about 180 liters of blood daily and produce about 1.5 liters of urine. About 1200 c.c. of blood flows through the kidneys per minute, which is nearly 1/5 of the blood pumped out by the heart in one minute.

stem: Which one among the following glands is present in pair in human body?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the human body, the adrenal gland is present in pairs. It is an endocrine gland found in vertebrates. It is located above the kidneys. Its function is to produce hormones that control important processes inside our body.

stem: The filtration unit in human kidney is called as a

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The filtration unit in the human kidney is called the nephron. It is used to separate water, ions, and small molecules from blood, filter wastes and toxic substances, and send necessary molecules back into the blood.

stem: in humans, the kidneys are part of which system?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In humans, the kidneys are a part of the excretion system. The kidneys filter liquid waste from the blood and form urine.

stem: Electroencephalogram (EEG) is used to monitor which of the following?

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

stem: Where is the governing centre of reflex action located?
expl: The control center of reflex actions is the spinal cord. The spinal cord is a cylindrical structure. Through it, we receive stimuli, and based on their nature, reflex actions are mainly of two types— (1) Unconditioned and (2) Conditioned. Due to reflex action, when the foot steps on a thorn, we immediately pull the foot backward.

expl: Macula and crista ampullaris present inside the ear maintain body balance. In addition, the cerebellum, also called the small brain, is a part of the hindbrain. It is also responsible for maintaining body balance and posture.

stem: input and output nerves meet at :
expl: Afferent (Sensory) and efferent (Motor) nerve impulses originated from the central nervous system. The central nervous system (CNS) is the processing center of the nervous system. The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord. The major functions of the CNS are processing information, controlling blood pressure and respiration, and regulating and coordinating body functions, etc. The CNS works like the central processing unit (CPU) of the body.

stem: Which of the following glands is called the 'third eye' of the human body?
expl: The Pineal gland is a very small gland located in the human brain, is called the “third eye” of the human body. It is the smallest endocrine gland in the human body. Its other names are conarium and epiphysis. It secretes the hormone melatonin, which plays a major role in regulating the body’s biological clock.

stem: Hormones are secreted by:
expl: Hormones are chemical messengers of the body, which regulate and coordinate many functions such as growth, metabolism, reproduction, water balance, blood pressure, etc. Hormones are secreted by endocrine glands. Reproductive glands (ovaries, testes) are also considered a part of the endocrine system because they also secrete hormones, but in general physiology, hormone secretion is collectively stated for endocrine glands

stem: Which of the following is a hormone?
expl: Insulin is an animal hormone secreted by the beta (β) cells of the islets of Langerhans of the endocrine part of the pancreas. In terms of chemical structure, insulin is a peptide hormone, formed from amino acids. It regulates the metabolism of glucose (carbohydrates), fats, and proteins in the body. Due to deficiency of insulin, a person suffers from diabetes.

options.label: e

expl: Oxytocin has two target tissues—the uterus and the mammary glands in females. After childbirth, this hormone helps the uterus return to its normal condition, and during lactation it contracts the myoepithelial cells of the mammary gland and increases milk ejection. Milk producers also give injections of artificial oxytocin to obtain more milk from cows and buffaloes; this injection/medicine is called Pitocin.

expl: The autonomic system is a part of the peripheral nervous system. It controls involuntary functions. Therefore, the development of the autonomic system can be defined as the self-regulatory activity.

expl: Estrogen is a hormone produced in females by the cells of the theca interna of Graafian follicles in the ovary, from puberty up to the age of menopause (about 45 to 55 years). stem: Sexual reproduction causes genetic variation because of -
expl: Genetic variation occurs through sexual reproduction due to gene blending, changes in chromosomes, and gene shuffling—all three.

stem: Where does fertilization occur?
expl: In humans, fertilization is internal. Through sexual intercourse, the male gamete (sperm) enters the female reproductive tract. Sperm are highly active and motile. Millions of sperm enter the vagina and move towards the uterus through the cervix. Finally, only one sperm fertilizes the ovum in the oviduct (fallopian tube).
